analysis: The code execution flow: 1) Parse command-line options using OptionParser. 2) If help option is present, print help and exit. 3) Extract host, port, password from parsed options. 4) Check password and non-option arguments for validity. 5) Build gRPC channel with host and port. 6) Create AuthHeaderCallCredentials with password. 7) Dispatch to getversion or getbalance command, making gRPC calls and formatting output. 8) If unknown command, print error and exit. Potential runtime exceptions: OptionParser.parse() may throw OptionException (runtime) if invalid options provided; ManagedChannelBuilder.build() may throw IllegalArgumentException if host/port invalid; gRPC stub calls (getVersion, getBalance) may throw StatusRuntimeException (runtime) on network or server errors; formatBalance internally divides by a constant non-zero, so no ArithmeticException. Currently, these runtime exceptions are unhandled, causing stack trace dumps on failure, which is user-unfriendly. Optimizing by catching these runtime exceptions centrally improves robustness and user experience. The best approach is to wrap the entire main logic (from parser creation to exit) in a try block and catch RuntimeException, which covers all unhandled runtime exceptions, printing an error message and exiting with failure.
